Hi Len

We are trying to compare farmland bird densities in the UK and NZ, using
line-transect surveys. The data from the UK comes from the British Trust=

for Ornithology=92s Breeding Bird Survey, while the NZ data comes from tw=
o
different surveys. We are using MCDS sampling, with the predominant habi=
tat
on each transect and the source of the data (for the NZ surveys) as
covariates. We are analyzing the NZ and UK datasets separately. We are
having trouble achieving convergence for some of the NZ models, particula=
rly
for models with habitat as the covariate. I have tried manually selectin=
g
the starting values for the model parameters, but this does not seem to f=
ix
the problem in most cases. In the attached project (for starlings in NZ)=
,
the model achieved convergence when the native woodland habitat was
excluded, but not when the exotic woodland habitat (with much fewer
observations) was excluded and native woodland included.

Any suggestions as to why the models are failing to converge, and
suggestions on how to achieve convergence would be greatly appreciated. =
If
the model fails to converge, how robust are the estimates from the analys=
is,
or are they invalid?

Thanks from your time, and thanks in advance for any advice you may come =
up
with!

Please note that I have attached the project as a zip file, but have rena=
med
the file extension as a .txt rather than a .zip to hopefully get around t=
he
email filters. You should just be able to rename it as a .zip file again=

for distance to open it (a previous posting to the list was rejected beca=
use
of the .zip extension.

Kind regards
Grant Blackwell
